display.title: No One Gets Lost: Reb Zalman Zezmer and the House in the Forest
display.summary_short: On the Alter Rebbe's yahrzeit: a Chassid collecting tzedakah gets lost in a forest and is trapped in a robbers' house, and learns that his detour was planned to bring a lost Jew back.
display.summary_long: For Chof-Daled Teves, the Alter Rebbe's yahrzeit, the storyteller explains the song's words 'every step is perfectly planned': the Baal Shem Tov taught that Hashem directs a person's footsteps, and wherever we arrive, even by 'getting lost', we are meant to do a mitzvah there. The Alter Rebbe sends his Chassid Reb Zalman Zezmer to collect tzedakah for poor families, warning him never to stay in a house whose doorway faces east. On the way home the wagon driver falls asleep, the horse wanders deep into a forest, and they knock at a lit house kept by an old Jew. Only when Reb Zalman asks which way is east does he realize his mistake. The old man locks them in, and a band of robbers arrives. All night Reb Zalman says Tehillim and calls out to his Rebbe. At dawn the old man frees them, saying they owe their lives to their Rebbe, and sends a banknote for the Rebbe. The Alter Rebbe explains that Hashem made Reb Zalman get lost to help a lost Jew return, and months later the old man comes back as a penitent. A short story of the Rebbe Rashab teaches that the Rebbe hears whenever we call.
display.lesson: Every step is planned by Hashem; wherever you end up, there is a mitzvah to do there. Whenever you call out to the Rebbe, the Rebbe hears.
